abstract: For nonempty Borel sets $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\Theta\subset O(d)\times\mathbb R^d$, where $d\ge2$, let $\Theta(E)$ be the union of the rigid copies $gE+z$, where $(g,z)\in\Theta$. We prove that $\Theta(E)$ has positive Lebesgue measure whenever $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E+\dim_H\Theta>\frac{d(d+1)}2$, where $\dim_{\mathrm{SF}} E$ is the spherical Fourier dimension of $E$. This resolves a conjecture on packing by arbitrary Borel families of rigid motions. Our proof develops a discrete-to-continuous framework by adapting a finite-field averaging argument to $\mathbb R^d$ using Sobolev estimates on the group of rigid motions. We also obtain analogous packing results for similarities. The same framework can be used to show that if $\tau$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the similarity group with finite $\bigl(\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1\bigr)$-energy, then every compactly supported $\tau$-stationary probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$ has a smooth density. We deduce that a nonempty compact set has nonempty interior if its family of similarity self-embeddings has Hausdorff dimension greater than $\frac{d(d-1)}{2}+1$.
hook: A set whose rigid copies are spread widely enough must cover positive volume when their dimensions add up.
summary: The authors prove that the union of rigid copies of a Borel set E over a family of motions has positive Lebesgue measure when the spherical Fourier dimension of E plus the family's Hausdorff dimension exceeds d(d+1)/2. This resolves a conjecture, with similar results for similarities. The method adapts a finite-field averaging argument using Sobolev estimates. It is a sufficient condition, not a sharp one in all cases.
title: Packing sets by rigid motions and similarities
